newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sets tax rule for natural resource transfers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sets tax rule for natural resource transfers.

text.p: Multinational companies will be protected from double taxation on income from natural resources produced outside the United States under a rule issued by the Internal Revenue Service Friday.

The rule was designed to ensure that large multinational companies would not have to change their calculations of taxable income from foreign sources under regulations that came into effect for the 1996 tax year, which required all affiliates of a multinational company to file a consolidated U.S. tax return.

Under the rule, "gross receipts equal to the fair market value of the product at the export terminal are allocated to the location of the farm, mine, well, deposit or uncut timber" whether it is in the United States or abroad, the IRS said.
Receipts that exceed a product's fair market value will be counted as income in the country of sale.
"It's important for the import of foreign-produced crude oil," an oil industry tax expert said.
Oil companies had been worried that under the consolidated tax filings, they would no longer be able to subtract some of their foreign tax payments from their U.S. taxable income.
By preserving existing regulations for reporting income from foreign production and extraction, Friday's rule protected multinationals from paying heavier taxes, the oil industry tax expert said.

But companies that produce liquefied natural gas (LNG) in the United States for export might face a bigger tax hit, because the IRS decided to treat liquefaction of natural gas as a manufacturing process instead of a production process.
Manufacturing processes cannot be subtracted as a cost when calculating the gross receipts from the sale of a natural resource.
